answer.rationale: The contract expires in 14 days with finance mandating an 18% spend cut, and the line runs at 94% with no buffer. Memory c4 confirms that renegotiating at renewal via benchmarking recovered real margin and moved the incumbent on price/payment terms—directly aligns with achieving the cost cut while retaining the incumbent. Memory c1 confirms that renewing with the incumbent preserves integration stability and delivery continuity, which is critical given the zero buffer. Together, these support negotiating new terms with the incumbent as the only path that simultaneously meets the 18% mandate and avoids increasing delivery risk. Switching vendors (c2) or adding a second source (c3) carries unacceptably high transition risk in a 14‑day window with no buffer; deferring (c5) violates the finance mandate; and bare renewal without negotiation likely fails the cost‑cut target.
